statements.sentence: On a test function that vanishes outside [-L, L], the prime-power side of the explicit formula, for any weights, is the finite sum over n up to e^L (primeTermQ_window, SIDE-explicit-formula v0.42 = 4964e957, run 44646848292, axioms [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound])
Below log 2 the prime sum of zeta's formula vanishes (primeSum_eq_zero_of_lt_log_two, SIDE-explicit-formula v0.42 = 4964e957, run 44646848292, axioms [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound])

On the autocorrelation of h the pole term is 2 Re(A conj B), twice the square of the integral of h cosh(x/2) on an even real h and minus twice the square of the integral of h sinh(x/2) on an odd one, and its real part is below 0 at a test function in classK (poleTerm_weilTest, poleTerm_weilTest_even, poleTerm_weilTest_odd and exists_classK_poleTerm_re_neg, SIDE-explicit-formula v0.42 = 4964e957, run 44646848292, axioms [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound])

For a real test function the form is the sum of its values on the even and the odd part (form_parity_split, SIDE-explicit-formula v0.42 = 4964e957, run 44646848292, axioms [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound])

At each width the weights for which the form is at or above 0 on each window of that width form a convex set fixed by the pole term and the archimedean term, and membership turns on finitely many weights (admissibleWeights_convex, admissibleWeights_congr and h2_sign_upto_iff_mem, SIDE-explicit-formula v0.42 = 4964e957, run 44646848292, axioms [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound])
